title: Give every number on the marketing site a source, by Fri 4 Dec
description: /solutions/bootcamps claims 50%, 2x and 40%; /solutions/universities claims 40%, 2x and 60%; /solutions/schools claims 50%, 2x and 65%. None carries a source, a sample or a date, and each page is under 450 words. Build one register of every quantitative claim on the public site: the exact wording, the page, what would prove it, and a supported or unsupported verdict. Then either attach the evidence or remove the number. No new statistic may be added without an entry.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Check the same numbers in the app, the decks and the press kit, because buyers meet them there too
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The website is the most visible surface, not the only one. The same 50% and 2x appear in decks, one-pagers and anything a salesperson sends after a call. Work: collect the numbers from the sales deck, the press kit and the in-app copy, put them against the register, and mark agreement, disagreement and numbers that exist nowhere else. Deliver the cross-surface table, the list to correct before the next send, and the note on which surface is authoritative when two disagree.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: For each number, write the smallest test that would prove it
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Roughly half of these claims could be proved with data the product already holds, and the other half never could. Work: for each claim in the register, write the measurement that would support it — which table, which period, which population, what would count as success — and mark the claims where the honest answer is "we have no way to know". Deliver the per-claim method, the three that could be measured this month, and the ones that must be replaced with a qualitative statement.
